record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The Definition admits zero morphisms and empty orthogonal sums in a fusion category, but excludes degenerate dagger positivity by f†f=0⇒f=0; evaluation/coevaluation need not be unitary isomorphisms.
Associator and unit constraints are structural maps, not an interval-valued family or a path with free endpoints.
Orthogonal semisimple decompositions are part of the finite-category structure; this Definition does not choose from an arbitrary indexed family of nonempty sets.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

## Definition

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category
$\mathcal C$ ([[def-qc-tqc-unitary-fusion-category]]). The **fusion
multiplicity** is

$$N_{ab}^c:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c),$$

and the corresponding **fusion multiplicity space** is

$$V_{ab}^c:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c).$$

Since $c$ is absolutely simple
([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]), each $f,g\in V_{ab}^c$ has a unique scalar
$\langle f,g\rangle$ satisfying
$f\circ g^\dagger=\langle f,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$. This fixes the
inner-product convention to be linear in the first variable. The next local
theorem proves that this pairing is positive definite. No multiplicity-free
assumption is made: $N_{ab}^c$ may be any nonnegative integer.

## Definition

A **unitary ribbon fusion category** is a unitary fusion category with a
unitary braiding and a ribbon structure in the sense of
[[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]. Thus the twist $\theta$ is a natural
automorphism of the identity satisfying the balancing identity and the
dual-compatibility condition of that root definition, and each component is
unitary: $\theta_X^\dagger=\theta_X^{-1}$. A ribbon structure is additional
data; it is not supplied by fusion rules or by a braid-group representation
alone.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: An underlying fusion category contains its zero object and empty direct sums; natural twist/braiding components there are the unique maps, while the tensor unit remains simple and nonzero.
The zero object is permitted by the underlying finite semisimple category; zero morphisms do not require an inverse as braidings/twists on nonzero objects do.

The Definition assumes a valid unitary ribbon structure and imposes no modular/nondegenerate-braiding condition; degenerate braiding is allowed, so a generic claim that degeneracy is excluded is not correct.
Balancing and dual compatibility are equations of natural transformations, not boundary values of a path.
The braiding and ribbon twist are supplied structure, not selections from a family of possible ribbon structures.
This is the definition of additional unitary ribbon data; it makes no theorem asserting that braid-group unitarity or fusion rules alone are equivalent to existence of a ribbon structure.

record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary ribbon fusion category. An object $x$ is
**transparent** if for every simple object $y$ the double braiding

$$c_{y,x}\circ c_{x,y}:x\otimes y\longrightarrow x\otimes y$$

is the identity. By naturality and additivity, the double braiding on a finite
direct sum is block diagonal with the double braidings on its simple summands;
therefore an object is transparent exactly when each simple summand is
transparent. Finite direct sums include the empty sum, so the zero object is
transparent. The category is **modular**, or **nondegenerate**, when its
transparent simple objects consist only of the tensor unit, equivalently when
its transparent objects are exactly the finite direct sums of the tensor unit.
This condition is additional to the existence of fusion spaces and a unitary
braid action.

record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

For a simple charge $a$ in a unitary ribbon fusion category, the twist
component is an endomorphism $\theta_a\in\operatorname{End}(a)$. Since
$\operatorname{End}(a)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_a$, there is a unique scalar
$\vartheta_a\in\mathbb C$ such that

$$\theta_a=\vartheta_a\operatorname{id}_a.$$

The scalar $\vartheta_a$ is the **topological spin** of $a$. Unitarity of the
twist gives
$|\vartheta_a|^2\operatorname{id}_a=\theta_a^\dagger\theta_a=\operatorname{id}_a$;
since $\operatorname{id}_a\ne0$, $|\vartheta_a|=1$.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: A simple a is nonzero and id_a≠0, so its unitary twist scalar cannot vanish; the proof explicitly uses this nonzero identity.
The scalar is attached to one simple charge, not a function of time or open-string endpoints.
Absolute simplicity gives a unique scalar coefficient; no representative among multiple possible coefficients is chosen.
The item derives |ϑ_a|=1 from the given unitary twist; it does not claim that an arbitrary unit-modulus assignment is sufficient to define a ribbon twist.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category and fix a set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ of representatives for the simple
isomorphism classes. Throughout this definition, the ordered input charges
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$, total charge $d$, and all internal edge charges are labels
in $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Also fix a parenthesized binary fusion
tree. At each internal vertex with incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge
$z$, choose one vector from an orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An
**admissible labeling** assigns a representative charge to each internal edge
so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a separate multiplicity-basis
index is retained at every vertex. Compose the vertex morphisms, inserting the
associators required by the chosen tree, to obtain a morphism from the
parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite morphisms are the
**fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a **fusion-tree basis** when it
is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space. For the
empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$ and its empty tree vector is
$\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$; for one input $a_1$, the
only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when $d=a_1$. The next local
lemma proves the basis property for every finite input list and includes the
dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

The term fusion-tree basis is assigned when the composed family is an orthonormal basis; this is a naming convention whose basis existence is proved by the subsequent lemma, not an extra characterization of arbitrary tensor categories.

## Definition

A **fusion-basis gauge change** chooses, for every triple of simple charges
$a,b,c$, a unitary matrix $G_{ab}^c$ changing the orthonormal basis of
$V_{ab}^c$. The convention is that the new basis columns are the old basis
columns multiplied by $G_{ab}^c$. On a recoupling block this gives

$$F'=G_R^{-1}FG_L,$$

where $G_L$ and $G_R$ are the direct sums of tensor products of the vertex
changes on the source and target trees. On an exchange block it gives

$$R'=(G_{ba}^c)^{-1}R G_{ab}^c.$$

The matrices change with the bases; the underlying categorical maps do not.

The source and target trees have distinct gauges G_L,G_R, and an exchange uses G_ab^c at source and G_ba^c at target; these endpoints cannot be silently identified.
The gauge matrices are supplied unitary basis changes in finitely many finite-dimensional multiplicity spaces, rather than an arbitrary-index choice principle.
The two coordinate transformation laws follow the stated basis convention; no converse that arbitrary matrices satisfying such laws realize a fusion category is claimed.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category, let $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$
be the representative set fixed in [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]], and take
$a_1,\ldots,a_n,d\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Fix any parenthesized
binary tree $T$ on the ordered input list. The fusion-tree vectors of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]] form an orthonormal basis of
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,d)$. Their number is

$$m_T(d)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\text{ admissible, with every internal label in }\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)}}\;\prod_{v\,\mathrm{internal}}N_{\ell(v_L)\,\ell(v_R)}^{\ell(v)},$$

where the leaves carry the inputs, the root carries $d$, and each internal edge
is labeled by a representative simple charge. For the left-associated tree on
$n$ inputs this gives $m_0(d)=1$ if $d=\mathbf1$ and $0$ otherwise,
$m_1(d)=1$ if $a_1=d$ and $0$ otherwise, and

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The last Definition sentence explicitly assigns an empty0×0 matrix to a zero-dimensional total fusion space; its channel sums can be empty.
Intermediate multiplicity-zero channels contribute no coordinates; nonzero multiplicities greater than one are all retained in the displayed indices.
The endpoints are Hom(((a⊗b)⊗c),d) and Hom(a⊗(b⊗c),d); inverse-precomposition fixes their direction.
Finite orthonormal vertex bases determine both tree bases; no selection over an arbitrary index class is used.
The equation defines coefficients of an already given associator; it does not claim the converse that arbitrary F coefficients define an associator satisfying the pentagon.

## Example

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

F/R table or global Ising ribbon coherence.

convention recording the eigenvalues of the object-level braiding itself, the
eigenvalues are the inverses of the displayed phases. This convention note
does not extend the sector data to any other Ising fusion space.

## Statement

Every F-symbol matrix in orthonormal fusion-tree bases of a unitary fusion
category is unitary.

record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category with associator $\alpha$ and
braiding $c$. For all objects $X,Y,Z$, its two hexagons are

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z} =(\operatorname{id}_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z} \circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes\operatorname{id}_Z),$$

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1} =(c_{X,Z}\otimes\operatorname{id}_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1} \circ(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

For simple input charges and a fixed simple total charge, the two route matrices
in each equation are equal in fusion-tree coordinates. Each entry is the sum
over all intermediate simple charges and multiplicity indices of the products
of the corresponding F- and R-block entries.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: If an intermediate fixed-total Hom space vanishes, its complete tree basis is empty and the finite matrix products/sums in the coordinate proof are empty-coordinate maps, with equal endpoint maps.
Some fusion channels may vanish and other multiplicities may exceed one; the proof sums all admissible simple labels and every vertex basis index.
The displayed braiding hexagon equation fixes the source and target parenthesizations. The proof explicitly chooses complete bases at both endpoints and all intermediate trees.
Only finitely many tree spaces and their already supplied finite bases occur along the two routes; there is no arbitrary indexed family selection.
Equality of the two braiding hexagon route matrices is derived from that categorical coherence axiom; no converse from one numerical sector to global categorical coherence is asserted.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category with associator $\alpha$ and
braiding $c$. For all objects $X,Y,Z$, its two hexagons are

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z} =(\operatorname{id}_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z} \circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes\operatorname{id}_Z),$$

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1} =(c_{X,Z}\otimes\operatorname{id}_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1} \circ(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

For simple input charges and a fixed simple total charge, the two route matrices
in each equation are equal in fusion-tree coordinates. Each entry is the sum
over all intermediate simple charges and multiplicity indices of the products
of the corresponding F- and R-block entries.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category. A finite list of simple
charges and total charge determines a fusion space in each parenthesization.
For a crossing word with underlying object map $b_\beta:P_L\to P_{L'}$, define
its action on the corresponding Hom spaces by
$f\mapsto f\circ b_\beta^{-1}$, from $\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d)$ to
$\operatorname{Hom}(P_{L'},d)$. Let $U_\beta$ be its matrix in chosen
fusion-tree bases. If each multiplicity basis is changed by the unitary
gauge matrices of [[def-qc-tqc-gauge-transform]], and $G_L,G_{L'}$ are the
induced source and target tree-basis unitaries, then

$$U_\beta'=G_{L'}^{-1}U_\beta G_L.$$

In particular, when $n\ge2$ and all $n$ strand charges are the same simple object $a$,
the adjacent exchanges act on the same fixed-total fusion space
$V=\operatorname{Hom}(a^{\otimes n},d)$, satisfy the Artin relations, and
define a unitary representation $\rho:B_n\to U(V)$, where $U(V)$ is the group
of invertible linear maps preserving the inner product on $V$.
If $V=0$, this is the unique action on the zero-dimensional space.
In that case $\rho'(\beta)=G_L^{-1}\rho(\beta)G_L$ for every braid $\beta$.
Thus basis-dependent matrix entries change, while the braid action up to
unitary equivalence and consistently transformed expectation values do not.

For the Fibonacci three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ sector and the Ising
three-$\sigma$, total-$\sigma$ sector, use the F/R data of
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]] and [[ex-qc-tqc-ising-data]]. In each sector the
first generator is $B_1=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,R_2)$ and the second is

The pair-first versus recoupled generator convention B1=diag(R1,R2), B2=FB1F is checked on each ordered channel basis in2.1–2.2.
Both F/R tables are supplied and all products are explicit; computing their Artin relation and order selects no family of witnesses.
The matrices are verified to satisfy Artin and stated projective orders; no converse characterizing all Ising/Fibonacci matrices by those relations is made.

record.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$\rho:B_n\to U(V)$ be a fixed mathematical braid representation. A **physical
implementation record** for a braid $b\in B_n$ consists of all of the following
data and hypotheses:

1. a finite-dimensional physical state space identified with $V$ on a specified
   low-energy sector;
2. a $C^2$ path $H(s)$ of Hermitian endomorphisms, $0\le s\le1$, and a
   norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ that
   is a coherently followed band in the sense of
   [[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]], including its local-contour
   continuation, and is separated from its complement by a uniform positive
   full gap;
3. an explicit initial preparation isometry into $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$,
   its declared preparation cost, and a stated slow-time schedule $T>0;$
4. a separate identification of the band's transported action for the chosen
   exchange path with $\rho(b)$, up to a stated scalar phase.

The first three clauses form an instance of the finite adiabatic path model
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]. Under those hypotheses,
[[thm-qa-36-jrs-finite-adiabatic-bound]] bounds the deviation from ideal
adiabatic band following. That estimate does not establish that a material
realizes the fusion category, that the exchange path has the prescribed
holonomy, or that the initial state can be prepared at no cost. Locality,
temperature, quasiparticle separation, stray excitations, and tunnelling
require their own physical error model.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The representation may be evaluated at the identity braid/empty word; V itself is explicitly nonzero and the path/preparation record remains required for an implementation.
V=0 and T=0 are excluded, and a positive full gap is required. The Definition does not assert gapless or zero-runtime adiabatic transport.
A nonzero1-dimensional low-energy sector is compatible with the record; no band rank greater than one is imposed.
The specified band has constant rank and a uniform positive full spectral gap; a rank jump or gap closing violates clause2.
The physical space, spectral path, preparation, schedule and holonomy identification are supplied record fields, not objects selected from an arbitrary family.

The record lists hypotheses for a physical implementation and explicitly says JRS does not prove the holonomy identification; no equivalence between a mathematical braid action and realizable hardware is claimed.

The record lists hypotheses for a physical implementation and explicitly says JRS does not prove the holonomy identification; no equivalence between a mathematical braid action and realizable hardware is claimed. In particular no reverse characterization is being imported from a dependency.

$\rho:B_n\to U(V)$ be a fixed mathematical braid representation. A **physical
implementation record** for a braid $b\in B_n$ consists of all of the following
data and hypotheses:

1. a finite-dimensional physical state space identified with $V$ on a specified
   low-energy sector;
2. a $C^2$ path $H(s)$ of Hermitian endomorphisms, $0\le s\le1$, and a
   norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ that
   is a coherently followed band in the sense of
   [[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]], including its local-contour
   continuation, and is separated from its complement by a uniform positive
   full gap;
3. an explicit initial preparation isometry into $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$,
   its declared preparation cost, and a stated slow-time schedule $T>0;$
4. a separate identification of the band's transported action for the chosen
   exchange path with $\rho(b)$, up to a stated scalar phase.

The first three clauses form an instance of the finite adiabatic path model
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]. Under those hypotheses,
[[thm-qa-36-jrs-finite-adiabatic-bound]] bounds the deviation from ideal
adiabatic band following. That estimate does not establish that a material
realizes the fusion category, that the exchange path has the prescribed
holonomy, or that the initial state can be prepared at no cost. Locality,
temperature, quasiparticle separation, stray excitations, and tunnelling
require their own physical error model.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The representation may be evaluated at the identity braid/empty word; V itself is explicitly nonzero and the path/preparation record remains required for an implementation.
V=0 and T=0 are excluded, and a positive full gap is required. The Definition does not assert gapless or zero-runtime adiabatic transport.
A nonzero1-dimensional low-energy sector is compatible with the record; no band rank greater than one is imposed.
The specified band has constant rank and a uniform positive full spectral gap; a rank jump or gap closing violates clause2.
The physical space, spectral path, preparation, schedule and holonomy identification are supplied record fields, not objects selected from an arbitrary family.

The record lists hypotheses for a physical implementation and explicitly says JRS does not prove the holonomy identification; no equivalence between a mathematical braid action and realizable hardware is claimed.

Fix a unitary fusion category $\mathcal D$ and the representative set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$ of [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]].
For an ordered list $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$,

parenthesized input tensor $T$, let $V=\operatorname{Hom}(T,c)\ne0$,
equipped with that definition's orthonormal fusion-tree inner product.
The identical-input case $x_1=\cdots=x_n=x$ retains the notation
$V=V(x^n\to c)$. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$

that subspace with an object of the fusion category.

## Definition

Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be a fixed-charge encoding, $P=JJ^*$ its code
projector, $U\in U(\mathcal C)$ a logical target, and $W\in U(V)$ an ambient
unitary. Its zero-on-the-complement target extension is
$\widetilde U:=JUJ^*:V\to V$. Define the **logical block error** and
**leakage amplitude** by
$$\epsilon_{\mathrm{log}}(W,U):=\|PWP-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{leak}}(W):=\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Both are finite operator norms. The first measures the compressed block
against the target; the second measures transfer from the code into its
orthogonal complement. They diagnose different errors.

## Definition

Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be a fixed-charge encoding, $P=JJ^*$ its code
projector, $U\in U(\mathcal C)$ a logical target, and $W\in U(V)$ an ambient
unitary. Its zero-on-the-complement target extension is
$\widetilde U:=JUJ^*:V\to V$. Define the **logical block error** and
**leakage amplitude** by
$$\epsilon_{\mathrm{log}}(W,U):=\|PWP-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{leak}}(W):=\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Both are finite operator norms. The first measures the compressed block
against the target; the second measures transfer from the code into its
orthogonal complement. They diagnose different errors.

## Definition

Fix a unitary braided fusion category $\mathcal C$ and the simple-object
representative set $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ used in
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Let $x,c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$,
let $n\ge2$, and suppose $V(x^n\to c)\ne0$. Use the left-associated fusion-tree basis. For the Artin
generator $\sigma_i$ that exchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st strands, let
$T_i$ be the specified sequence of $F$-moves that changes from the fixed tree
basis to a basis where those two charges fuse first, and let $R_i$ apply the
corresponding $R$-symbol on each pair-charge channel. Define
$$\rho_c(\sigma_i):=T_i^{-1}R_iT_i.$$
This defines the generator assignment. The next theorem proves that the
assignment descends from words to a well-defined group homomorphism. Word
products use matrix multiplication acting right-to-left on column vectors.
The abstract group in this definition is the Artin group
[[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]; the positive crossing is the
generator convention used for the displayed $R$-symbols. If a motion is
described chronologically, its matrix product is written in reverse temporal
order.

## Definition

Let $m\ge2$ and let $\mathcal H=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$. A **Majorana
system of length $2m$** is a family of operators
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ satisfying
$$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j^2=I,\qquad \gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j\quad(j\ne k).$$
Its parity operator is $\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$. For each adjacent
pair, put
$$Q_1(j)=\frac{I-i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad Q_\psi(j)=\frac{I+i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad U_j=\exp\!\left(-\frac\pi4\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}\right).$$

A **Majorana–Ising exchange interface** on a fixed parity sector consists of
such a system, a choice $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ and the sector
$\mathcal H_\eta=\ker(\Pi-\eta I)$, together with the following explicit
model-identification hypotheses for every $1\le j<2m$: the Ising pair-charge
projections are identified with $Q_1(j),Q_\psi(j)$, and the exchange is
$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)$ with the same relative phase
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. The last identity is required for all adjacent pairs as part
of the interface; the three-anyon supplier below establishes it only in its
stated sector and does not prove this all-$m$ identification.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The family has exactly2m≥4 specified Majorana operators on a2^m-dimensional register. The word family does not admit an empty index set here; the regex flag is a false positive.

## Definition

Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$U(V)$ be its unitary group. Two unitaries are **projectively equivalent**
when $A=zB$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with $|z|=1$; write $[A]\in PU(V)$ for
the equivalence class. Define
$$d_P([A],[B]):=\min_{|z|=1}\|A-zB\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This is the distance after quotienting by one common scalar phase. The phase
is minimized over the unit circle; it is not chosen independently in
different charge blocks.

Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$U(V)$ be its unitary group. Two unitaries are **projectively equivalent**
when $A=zB$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with $|z|=1$; write $[A]\in PU(V)$ for
the equivalence class. Define
$$d_P([A],[B]):=\min_{|z|=1}\|A-zB\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This is the distance after quotienting by one common scalar phase. The phase
is minimized over the unit circle; it is not chosen independently in
different charge blocks.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The unit circle over which phases are minimized is nonempty and V≠0; the compact-minimum domain is never an empty set.
For dimV=1 every unitary is scalar, so PU(V) is a singleton and the same minimum metric has value0; no dimV≥2 hypothesis is imposed.
Scalar-related A,B give zero quotient distance; proof1.2 and3.1 show this is a genuine metric on classes rather than a degenerate metric on representatives.
The minimizing domain is the unit circle, with no chosen interval endpoints; its compactness in2.1 does not impose a path endpoint convention.
The compact unit circle is nonempty by[F3] and2.1, so its continuous norm-distance function has a minimizing phase. Proof3.1 chooses two such minimizers, a finite selection, not arbitrary-index AC.

## Definition

Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6}) \circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6} \circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$
from the triple-grouped input tree to the left-associated tree. On a fusion
morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

For one triple of total charge $\tau$, its two orthonormal path vectors are
indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle: x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$
In the ordered basis
$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.
The same ordered local triple paths are used for $a=1$ and $a=\tau$; only
the final pair-charge coordinate differs. The orthogonal complements are
called leakage spaces.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Both explicitly enumerated fixed-total sectors are nonzero with dimensions5 and8, and each code has four specified path vectors. Being indexed by x,y∈{1,τ} is not an empty-family quantifier.
The selected code ranks and both leakage-complement dimensions are positive; no zero-dimensional sector or zero code is included in this fixed six-anyon calculation.
Proof2.1 explicitly identifies the total-unit sector leakage complement as1-dimensional; proof1.1 also uses multiplicity-one vertex channels.
This fixed Fibonacci construction has rank4 codes with complement dimensions1 and4, not a varying-rank family or arbitrary singular encoding.
The Definition types g from the grouped six-input tree to the left-associated tree and G_a by inverse-precomposition, retaining the same simple total a∈{1,τ}.
The four ordered code paths and finite associator sequence are fixed; the resulting isometry follows from their orthonormality, with only finite choices.
The construction and dimension proof do not identify the triple code with every other four-dimensional subspace or characterize category objects by projector rank.

## Definition

Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6}) \circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6} \circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$
from the triple-grouped input tree to the left-associated tree. On a fusion
morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

For one triple of total charge $\tau$, its two orthonormal path vectors are
indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle: x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$
In the ordered basis
$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.
The same ordered local triple paths are used for $a=1$ and $a=\tau$; only
the final pair-charge coordinate differs. The orthogonal complements are
called leakage spaces.

This fixed Fibonacci construction has rank4 codes with complement dimensions1 and4, not a varying-rank family or arbitrary singular encoding.

## Example

For three $\tau$ anyons of total charge $\tau$, the fusion space is
two-dimensional. Fix the chiral convention
$$F=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\ \phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}.$$
After removing the common scalar $R_1$, the adjacent generators are
$$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r),\qquad B_2=FB_1F.$$

The verification checks these matrices directly as a unitary $B_3$
representation. It uses the listed sector data as input and does not infer
global category coherence from this calculation.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The Fibonacci example fixes a nonzero2-dimensional three-anyon sector and two adjacent generators; it has no empty input list.
The sector and displayed unitary matrices are fixed and nonzero; zero total-space or zero-parameter specializations are not among these worked inputs.
The two channel maps are scalar multiplicity-one blocks inside the displayed2-dimensional sector; the proof explicitly computes their unit-modulus phases.
The Fibonacci F matrix and phase ratio are fixed invertible data; no coalescing, singular or variable-rank case is asserted.
The example fixes ordered pair channels and distinguishes the first adjacent generator from the F-recoupled second one; it does not change the total charge.
Every Fibonacci matrix and basis label is supplied explicitly, so the verification uses no unspecified selection.
This is a verification of the specified Fibonacci matrices, not an equivalence classifying all braid representations by their noncommutation property.

## Statement

Fix the Fibonacci convention with common exchange scalar $R_1$. Let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be exponent sum, sending each Artin generator $\sigma_i$
to $1$. If $\widetilde\rho$ is the generator-normalized representation
$\widetilde\rho(\sigma_i)=R_1^{-1}\rho(\sigma_i)$, then for every braid $b$
and every total-charge block,
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}\widetilde\rho(b).$$
The scalar is the same on every total-charge block and every spectator
multiplicity. It is a global phase for an uncontrolled fixed-sector
computation; under coherent control it is a relative phase and must be
tracked.

## Statement

Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}= \begin{cases} \sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}}, &x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.

## Statement

Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}= \begin{cases} \sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}}, &x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.

## Statement

Let $r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$, $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2=1-r-r^{-1}$, and
$s=\sqrt\phi>0$. Then
$$\mathbb Z[r,s]\cong \mathbb Z[x,y]\big/\bigl(x^4-x^3+x^2-x+1,\ y^2-(1-x-x^{-1})\bigr),$$
where $x^{-1}=x^9$. The assignment
$$r\mapsto15,\qquad r^{-1}\mapsto29,\qquad \phi\mapsto19,\qquad s\mapsto9$$
defines a ring homomorphism to $\mathbb F_{31}$. The elements $r$ and
$\phi$ map to nonzero units, and conjugation of coefficients is handled by
$r\mapsto r^{-1}$ before reduction.

Proof3.1 checks the defining polynomial relations reduce to zero modulo31, while r andφ reduce to nonzero15 and19, so their denominator inverses remain valid.
The assignment preserves the ring unit and3.1 explicitly uses 1−15−29=19; this is a unital specialization, not a variable dimension-one theorem.
The chosen algebraic embedding has φ>0 and r≠0; the finite-field image keeps r andφ nonzero, excluding a singular denominator specialization.
No interval is present: r is the fixed primitive tenth root and s its fixed positive real square root, with conjugation prescribed before reduction.
Both the complex root and the finite-field images15,29,19,9 are fixed, so no arbitrary root or embedding selection is hidden.
The proof establishes the displayed ring presentation and one homomorphism; it does not classify every prime or every finite-field specialization by the converse of those assignments.

Let $P$ be a code projection on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $V$. Let
$W_1,\ldots,W_G$ be ideal unitaries preserving $\operatorname{ran}P$, and let
$V_1,\ldots,V_G$ be physical unitaries with
$\|V_j-W_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_j$. If
$V_{\mathrm{tot}}=V_G\cdots V_1$ and $W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_G\cdots W_1$,
then, with empty products equal to $I$ and empty sums equal to $0$,
$$\|V_{\mathrm{tot}}-W_{\mathrm{tot}}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le\sum_{j=1}^{G}\delta_j.$$

code action of $W_{\mathrm{tot}}$ are each at most $\sum_j\delta_j$.

## Definition

Let $\Gamma\le U(V)$ be a subgroup acting on a nonzero finite-dimensional
Hilbert space $V$. It is **exactly universal** on $V$ when $\Gamma=U(V)$,
**projectively exactly universal** when its image in $PU(V)$ is all of
$PU(V)$, and **projectively dense** when that image is dense in the metric
$d_P$ of [[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]].

For an encoding $J:\mathcal C\to V$ with code projector $P=JJ^*$, the action
is **approximate logical-and-leakage universal** if for every
$U\in U(\mathcal C)$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is $W\in\Gamma$ and a
phase $z\in U(1)$ such that
$$\|PWP-zJUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
This last notion includes a leakage bound as a separate requirement; projective
density on one fusion block alone does not supply it.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Γ is a subgroup and hence contains the identity/empty word when given by braids; the ambient/code spaces remain nonzero under the encoding convention.
Approximate universality quantifies ε>0 only and does not promise an exactly zero-error leakage-free gate; zero ambient V is excluded.
Dimension-one V is permitted; then its projective group is a singleton, though exact U(1) universality and the code conditions retain their own definitions.
A full-code encoding may have zero leakage complement, making the leakage inequality identically zero; the Definition imposes no nonzero complement.
The notions quantify target unitaries and error tolerances, not a path with endpoints.
Each target/tolerance asks for existence of a word and a phase; no simultaneously chosen function over all targets or arbitrary-index choice is asserted.

The item gives separate definitions of exact, projective and code/leakage universality and explicitly warns that density on one block does not supply the leakage criterion; no equivalence between those notions is claimed.

In particular no reverse characterization is being imported from a dependency.

## Definition

Let $\Gamma\le U(V)$ be a subgroup acting on a nonzero finite-dimensional
Hilbert space $V$. It is **exactly universal** on $V$ when $\Gamma=U(V)$,
**projectively exactly universal** when its image in $PU(V)$ is all of
$PU(V)$, and **projectively dense** when that image is dense in the metric
$d_P$ of [[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]].

For an encoding $J:\mathcal C\to V$ with code projector $P=JJ^*$, the action
is **approximate logical-and-leakage universal** if for every
$U\in U(\mathcal C)$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is $W\in\Gamma$ and a
phase $z\in U(1)$ such that
$$\|PWP-zJUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
This last notion includes a leakage bound as a separate requirement; projective
density on one fusion block alone does not supply it.

A full-code encoding may have zero leakage complement, making the leakage inequality identically zero; the Definition imposes no nonzero complement.

three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ fusion space from

in $PU(2)$.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient by
$\{\pm I\}$, and let $\Gamma\le PU(2)$ be dense. Then the full inverse image
$q^{-1}(\Gamma)$ is dense in $SU(2)$. Thus projective density gives
determinant-one lifts arbitrarily close to any $SU(2)$ target, while the
choice of a lift can differ by the central sign.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Proof1.1 begins with an arbitrary nonempty open O; its sheet intersection and image N are nonempty because they contain the chosen lift and its image. No witness is demanded for O=∅.
The target groups are SU(2) and PU(2), with kernel±I; there is no zero-dimensional or zero-matrix covering fiber.
The covering has two sheets over fixed2×2 groups; the result does not include a variable SU(1) branch.
The supplied map is an unbranched two-sheet covering;1.1 shrinks to a homeomorphic sheet rather than allowing a collapsed fiber.
The proof uses open neighborhoods and local sheets, not paths with prescribed endpoints.
ACω is carried from the covering/density suppliers. For a given nonempty O,1.1 and2.1 choose only a point and one element of N∩Γ, not simultaneous choices for all open sets.
The implication used is density of Γ⇒density of its full two-sheet inverse image; no converse about density of an arbitrary selected set of one lift per fiber is asserted.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient by
$\{\pm I\}$, and let $\Gamma\le PU(2)$ be dense. Then the full inverse image
$q^{-1}(\Gamma)$ is dense in $SU(2)$. Thus projective density gives
determinant-one lifts arbitrarily close to any $SU(2)$ target, while the
choice of a lift can differ by the central sign.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Proof1.1 begins with an arbitrary nonempty open O; its sheet intersection and image N are nonempty because they contain the chosen lift and its image. No witness is demanded for O=∅.
The target groups are SU(2) and PU(2), with kernel±I; there is no zero-dimensional or zero-matrix covering fiber.
The covering has two sheets over fixed2×2 groups; the result does not include a variable SU(1) branch.
The supplied map is an unbranched two-sheet covering;1.1 shrinks to a homeomorphic sheet rather than allowing a collapsed fiber.
The proof uses open neighborhoods and local sheets, not paths with prescribed endpoints.
ACω is carried from the covering/density suppliers. For a given nonempty O,1.1 and2.1 choose only a point and one element of N∩Γ, not simultaneous choices for all open sets.
The implication used is density of Γ⇒density of its full two-sheet inverse image; no converse about density of an arbitrary selected set of one lift per fiber is asserted.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U\in U(\mathbb C^4)$ and $\delta>0$.
There is one normalized six-strand Fibonacci braid word $b$ such that its
actions $B_1(b)$ and $B_\tau(b)$ on the total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
blocks are simultaneously within $\delta$ of
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For the triple-triple computational subspace in either block, the logical
block error and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$. The corresponding
physical categorical braid differs from the normalized word by the common
scalar phase specified by
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]].

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The identity target U=I4 has identity extensions and permits the empty braid; the theorem itself requires six strands and nonzero5/8-dimensional blocks.
The approximation parameter is δ>0. The theorem does not infer an exact zero-error leakage-free word for every U from density.
Proof1.1 uses the one-dimensional leakage complement in the total-unit block, with scalar(detU)^-1; the totalτ complement has four dimensions.
U with detU=1 makes the correcting scalar1; proof1.1 still gives valid unitary determinant-one extensions. No nonzero phase angle is required.
The two target blocks are compared by operator norm, with no varying path endpoints or braid strand endpoints.
Proof2.1 chooses one word from a nonempty product neighborhood supplied by joint density under ACω, rather than separately selecting words in each sector.
A common full-block approximation implies logical and leakage bounds; neither those weaker bounds nor separate block density is asserted equivalent to the simultaneous claim.

A common full-block approximation implies logical and leakage bounds; neither those weaker bounds nor separate block density is asserted equivalent to the simultaneous claim. In particular no reverse characterization is being imported from a dependency.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U\in U(\mathbb C^4)$ and $\delta>0$.
There is one normalized six-strand Fibonacci braid word $b$ such that its
actions $B_1(b)$ and $B_\tau(b)$ on the total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
blocks are simultaneously within $\delta$ of
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For the triple-triple computational subspace in either block, the logical
block error and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$. The corresponding
physical categorical braid differs from the normalized word by the common
scalar phase specified by
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]].

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The identity target U=I4 has identity extensions and permits the empty braid; the theorem itself requires six strands and nonzero5/8-dimensional blocks.
The approximation parameter is δ>0. The theorem does not infer an exact zero-error leakage-free word for every U from density.
Proof1.1 uses the one-dimensional leakage complement in the total-unit block, with scalar(detU)^-1; the totalτ complement has four dimensions.
U with detU=1 makes the correcting scalar1; proof1.1 still gives valid unitary determinant-one extensions. No nonzero phase angle is required.
The two target blocks are compared by operator norm, with no varying path endpoints or braid strand endpoints.
Proof2.1 chooses one word from a nonempty product neighborhood supplied by joint density under ACω, rather than separately selecting words in each sector.
A common full-block approximation implies logical and leakage bounds; neither those weaker bounds nor separate block density is asserted equivalent to the simultaneous claim.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $n\ge2$, and a total-charge label $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$. The code in $3n$ $\tau$ anyons factors as
$\mathcal C_n\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$.
For any adjacent pair of encoded triples, any $U\in U(4)$, and any
$\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid induces an ambient operator
within $\delta$ of the code-preserving ideal extension of $U$ on the entire
fixed-charge space $V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$. Consequently its logical block error
and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$, uniformly over all
spectator fusion paths and states that already have a component outside the
code.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $n\ge1$, every total-charge label $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, every unitary $U$ on $n$ logical qubits, and every
$\epsilon>0$, the triple-$\tau$ code
$$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$$
admits a finite normalized braid word $V_b$ such that
$$\inf_{|z|=1}\|P_{\rm code}V_bP_{\rm code} -zJ(U\otimes I_S)J^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P_{\rm code})V_bP_{\rm code}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
Here $S=V(\tau^n\to c)$ is the spectator space, $J:(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes S\to V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ is the isometric triple-code inclusion, and the logical target is lifted as $U\otimes I_S$. The bounds are uniform over spectator fusion states. No efficient braid
word-length, search-time, or finite-precision bound is asserted.

## Example

In a Majorana–Ising realization satisfying
[[def-qc-tqc-ising-majorana-interface]], braid-only gates on a fixed parity
sector normalize the logical Pauli group and form a finite projective
Clifford subgroup. In the
three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ Fibonacci sector, the two braid generators instead
generate a subgroup dense in $PU(2)$. The models therefore have different
projective gate power even though both use unitary braid matrices.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Both compared models have nonzero represented sectors and specified braid generators; no empty model is used as the comparison.
The comparison varies neither an error parameter through zero nor a zero-dimensional Hilbert space; the groups are the stated finite and infinite projective images.
The Fibonacci side is one logical qubit in a2-dimensional sector, and the Majorana side includes m=2, also one encoded qubit.
The Ising conclusion assumes the all-adjacent Majorana interface; dropping it is outside the example, not a degenerate case proved from a single Ising sector.
The comparison is of subgroup closures and gate power, not open paths or temporal endpoint values.
ACω is explicitly inherited for the Fibonacci density result; the Ising finite-group argument adds no choice principle.
The example contrasts two supplied models and makes no equivalence between unitarity of braid matrices and dense projective computational power.

The example contrasts two supplied models and makes no equivalence between unitarity of braid matrices and dense projective computational power. In particular no reverse characterization is being imported from a dependency.

## Example

The exact B6 certificates have determinants $17$ and $22$ modulo $31$ for
the selected $24\times24$ and $63\times63$ Lie-word minors. In the
total-charge-$1$ six-anyon space there are two natural four-dimensional code
choices: a pair-charge code and the triple code of
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]. The density argument applies to
either chosen subspace; the two definitions use different fusion trees, and
no equality of their projectors is asserted. For a circuit with $G>0$ ideal
one-qubit or adjacent two-qubit gates, assigning $\delta_j=\epsilon/G$
gives total logical block error and leakage at most $\epsilon$.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The circuit budget explicitly assumes G>0 before dividing ε/G; the example does not claim that formula for an empty circuit.
Proof4.1 distinguishes exact logical block equality, which forces zero leakage, from Wθ with positive1−cosθ and sinθ for0<θ<π/2.
Proof1.1–1.2 uses the one-dimensional complement of either four-dimensional charge1 code;4.1 also gives an explicit one-dimensional logical-code rotation witness.
The determinant-correction construction covers detU_j=1 as scalar1; the two distinct four-dimensional codes are not identified even if they share their ambient dimension.
The rotation witness in4.1 restricts0<θ<π/2; θ=0 andπ/2 are not the claimed strict-angle example. Ordered path basis choices in2.1 fix each code/complement target.
Under ACω, proof3.1 chooses finitely many common words from nonempty joint neighborhoods, using actual ambient SU5/SU8 targets constructed in2.1.

The example explicitly avoids a projector-equality claim for pair and triple codes; it proves density guarantees for either chosen code, not a converse equating code definitions from their common rank.

## Definition

Fix an integer $L\ge3$ and write $\mathbb Z_L=\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$. The
periodic square cellulation has vertices $q_{i,j}$, horizontal edges $h_{i,j}$
from $q_{i,j}$ to $q_{i+1,j}$, vertical edges $v_{i,j}$ from $q_{i,j}$ to
$q_{i,j+1}$, and faces $f_{i,j}$, for $i,j\in\mathbb Z_L$. Every index is
read modulo $L$. The boundary of $f_{i,j}$ consists of
$h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},h_{i,j+1},v_{i,j}$. Equivalently, this is the quotient of
the unit square tiling of $\mathbb R^2$ by translations in $L\mathbb Z^2$.

The cellulation has $L^2$ vertices, $2L^2$ edges, and $L^2$ faces. The
condition $L\ge3$ ensures that the four edges in each star and face are
distinct, and that every edge has two distinct endpoints and two distinct
incident faces. The vertex-edge graph joins vertices joined by an edge. The
face-adjacency graph joins faces sharing an edge; both graphs are connected.

## Statement

Write the torus as $T_L=\mathbb R^2/(L\mathbb Z^2)$ with its periodic
square cellulation. Let $D\subset T_L$ be a nonempty compact embedded
topological disk with connected complement. Then the quotient map
$\pi:\mathbb R^2\to T_L$ has a lift $\widetilde D\subset\mathbb R^2$ on
which it is one-to-one and maps $\widetilde D$ homeomorphically onto $D$.
Consequently every finite primal or dual edge chain supported in $D$ lifts
to a finite chain in the infinite square tiling, and cycles lift to cycles.

## Statement

Let $Z_1$ be the space of primal edge chains with even incidence at every
vertex, and let $B_1$ be the span of the face boundaries. Then $B_1\subseteq
Z_1$, the quotient $Z_1/B_1$ has dimension two, and the two winding
parities give coordinates on that quotient. The same statement holds for
dual edge chains, with dual vertex boundaries in place of face boundaries.
The horizontal loop $\gamma_h=\sum_i h_{i,0}$ has winding pair $(1,0)$,
and the vertical loop $\gamma_v=\sum_j v_{0,j}$ has pair $(0,1)$; their dual
counterparts give the corresponding basis of the dual quotient.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The zero/empty edge chain is a cycle and lies inB1. The tree-elimination argument in1.1 terminates at the zero chain when no non-tree coefficients remain.
A fundamental horizontal or vertical loop has exactly one winding coordinate equal to1 and the other0, computed in3.1.
The finite periodic cellulation has L≥3; independent nonzero winding loops rule out a collapsed quotient of dimension0 or1.
A non-tree edge closes the unique tree path between its endpoints in1.1; open chains with unmatched endpoint incidence are not inZ1.
The spanning tree is explicitly given; its unique finite endpoint paths define each fundamental cycle, so only finite constructions are used.
Proof2.1 shows every primal boundary has both winding parities0, and the identical dual calculation gives the forward implication.
Proof3.1 proves the quotient has the two independent fundamental winding classes as basis, so a cycle with both winding coordinates0 lies inB1; the dual argument is identical.

## Statement

Delete the star $A_{0,0}$ and plaquette $B_{0,0}$ from the full check list,
and call the remaining $r=2L^2-2$ checks $g_1,\ldots,g_r$. They are
independent commuting Hermitian involutions. For each sign string
$s\in\mathbb F_2^r$, the operator

$$P_s=\prod_{a=1}^r\frac{I+(-1)^{s_a}g_a}{2}$$

is the orthogonal projection onto the corresponding joint eigenspace; the
$P_s$ are pairwise orthogonal and sum to the identity. The omitted checks
are determined by the retained ones, so every nonzero syndrome sector has
an even number of e defects and an even number of m defects.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Proof1.1 says an identity-support product of retained checks must select empty star and plaquette subsets;2.1 explicitly permits zero projectors/empty eigenspaces.
The zero sign string is admitted, as are zero projectors before their ranks are established;2.1 includes zero summands in the orthogonal resolution.
Each one-check factor(I±g_a)/2 is a projection by1.1, and a differing single sign forces P_sP_t=0 in2.1.
Step2.1 explicitly allows zero projections; it does not assume every joint eigenspace has positive dimension before invoking the later code-dimension result.
The index s is a finite sign string, not an open spatial trail or time path; no external endpoint parameter is present.
For s≠t,2.1 chooses one differing coordinate from a finite nonempty difference set; no arbitrary-family choice is required.
Proof3.1: the total check-sign product is+1, so the number of negative signs in each species is even.

The finite sign calculation in3.1 has product+1 exactly when the number of minus signs is even; this converse is about sign parity, not a claim that every arbitrary prescribed syndrome is physically realizable.

## Statement

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric checks with $L\ge3$, the common $+1$
eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on $n=2L^2$ qubits. Its independent
check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is
$2^{n-r}=4=2^2$ and it encodes two logical qubits.

## Definition

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

## Statement

For the finite toric-code Hamiltonian
$H_L=-J_e\sum_q A_q-J_m\sum_f B_f$ with $J_e,J_m>0$, the ground space is
the four-dimensional toric code space and the ground energy is
$E_g=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$. The exact spectral gap above it is
$\Delta_L=4\min(J_e,J_m)$.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The all-positive sector has empty defect sets and is the4-dimensional ground code in2.1.
Ground-sector defect counts areN_e=N_m=0; the positive-gap claim concerns other nonzero sectors, with each present species having at least two defects.
The equal-coupling case J_e=J_m is included in the J_e≤J_m branch of3.1, with gap4J_e; zero couplings remain excluded.
The one-edge paths in3.1 have distinct endpoints supplied by L≥3, giving two defects; no open-system boundary is introduced.
Step3.1 chooses one edge and one nonzero code vector from known finite nonempty sets/spaces, with no arbitrary indexed choice.
The theorem derives the exact unperturbed finite-volume gap; a positive gap is not asserted equivalent to perturbation stability or thermal memory protection.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be the periodic toric code and let $\Pi$ be its orthogonal
code projector. Let $D$ be a compact embedded disk in the torus with
connected complement. Let $S\subseteq E_L$ be a set of edge qubits such that
$D$ contains both the primal edge segment and its crossing dual edge segment
for every $e\in S$. Then every operator $O$ supported on $S$ has scalar compression
to the code:

$$\Pi O\Pi=c(O)\Pi$$

for some $c(O)\in\mathbb C$.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: A one-edge support inside the stated disk is included; its supported operator is expanded inI,X,Y,Z in1.1 before the same compression argument.
A noncontractible region or support whose crossing dual segments leaveD does not meet the hypotheses; the theorem makes no such disk-degeneracy extension.

Proof2.1 distinguishes an anticommuting open-syndrome Pauli with zero compression from commuting primal/dual cycles. The disk lift preserves their closed incidence; no noncontractible or unmatched-endpoint support is included.
For each finite Pauli term the proof uses a finite lifted face chain from the explicit square-grid supplier; no arbitrary selection of regions or cycles is made.
Disk-supported operators are proved to have scalar compression. The converse that every operator with scalar compression has disk support is not asserted.

## Statement

Let $P$ be a primal path and $Q$ a dual path whose edge supports share
exactly one physical qubit. Then their string Paulis anticommute:
$Z(P)X(Q)=-X(Q)Z(P)$. This is the algebraic mutual e/m string sign.

Zero overlap is outside the stated one-crossing theorem; it would give commuting rather than the claimed anticommuting sign.
Exactly one shared physical qubit is the explicit hypothesis, and proof1.1 evaluates(-1)^1=−1.
The proof assumes actual Pauli strings and a single shared physical qubit, not coincident arbitrary trajectories or a singular Hamiltonian limit.
The paths may be open, but proof1.1 uses only their overlap parity; no prescribed endpoint locations or endpoint exchange dynamics are inferred.
The two string supports are given and their one-qubit overlap is counted directly.
A single overlap is sufficient for anticommutation; the theorem does not state the false converse that anticommutation requires exactly one overlap rather than any odd overlap.

## Definition

Fix $L\ge3$, $J_e,J_m>0$, a unit vector $\psi$ in the toric code space, and
a specified nontrivial logical Pauli representative $Q$. An **elementary
Pauli path to $Q$** is a finite sequence $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ with $E_0=I$,
$E_T$ a scalar-phase multiple of $Q$, and
$E_{r+1}=P_rE_r$, where each $P_r$ is $X$, $Y$, or $Z$ on a single edge and
the identity on every other edge.

For any prefix Pauli $E$, define its energy excess
$\varepsilon(E):=\langle E\psi,H_LE\psi\rangle-E_{\rm code}$, where
$E_{\rm code}:=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$ is the energy of every code vector. The
**Pauli-path energy barrier** of $Q$ is

$$\mathcal B_L(Q):=\min_{(E_0,\ldots,E_T)}\max_{0\le r\le T}\varepsilon(E_r),$$

where the minimum ranges over elementary Pauli paths to $Q$. This is a
finite-code energy quantity; it is not a thermal lifetime.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: One-edge Pauli steps are the allowed elementary updates; a prefix may contain a single error and its syndrome energy is covered by1.1–2.1.
The specified logical class is nontrivial and couplings are positive; an identity target or zero coupling is not the stated barrier problem.
The Definition fixes E0=I and ET equal to a phase multiple of the nontrivial logicalQ. Verification1.2 constructs at least one finite path between those endpoints;2.1 proves the minimum peak exists.
The Definition defines a minimax energy quantity and proves its existence, not a biconditional between small energy barrier and thermal lifetime.
The explicitly declared finite-code barrier is not a thermal lifetime, and no converse turns a dynamical lifetime claim into a minimax bound.

## Statement

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric stabilizer code with $L\ge3$, the
minimum weight of a normalizer Pauli outside the scalar-phase stabilizer is
$d(S)=L$.

A scalar-phase stabilizer/zero logical class is excluded by N(S)\Z_nS, and3.1 supplies a positive-weight nontrivial loop.

Proof1.1 forces even primal/dual incidences from check commutation, so the relevant supports are cycles without unmatched endpoints.
The lower-bound argument fixes an arbitrary nontrivial logical Pauli;3.1 supplies the explicitly defined horizontal loop to make the finite minimum set nonempty.
The theorem proves d(S)=L by lower and upper bounds; it does not classify all weight-L Paulis as nontrivial logicals or assert a converse geometric reconstruction.

## Statement

For each finite $L\ge3$, the toric Hamiltonian has an exact positive gap,
contractible-disk local indistinguishability, and a constant upper bound on a
logical-string energy barrier. These unperturbed facts alone do not imply
stability under arbitrary perturbations: the explicit global-projector
perturbation $V_L=-\Delta_L(I-\Pi_L)$ closes the gap above the original
code space and enlarges the ground space, where $\Pi_L$ is the ground
projector and $\Delta_L=4\min(J_e,J_m)$. This does not refute
stability theorems for sufficiently small local perturbations, and it makes
no claim about thermal dynamics or a material realization.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The code and its orthogonal complement are both nonzero;1.1 uses full dimension2^{2L²}>4, so no empty excited sector supplies the witness.
Proof3.1 makes the energy gap above the original four-dimensional code exactly zero after adding the explicit global perturbation.
Proof1.1 uses the first excited eigenspace at E_g+Δ; shifting that level byΔ in3.1 suffices without assuming it is one-dimensional.
The perturbed ground eigenspace is strictly larger than the original code, which is the intentional spectral degeneracy of the counterexample.
There is no perturbation interpolation parameter with endpoints; one fixed global projector perturbation is constructed.
The finite nonzero excited complement has a least eigenvalue by1.1; the projector perturbation is then explicit, not an arbitrary selected material error.
The example refutes an implication from unperturbed finite facts to stability under arbitrary perturbations; it does not state an equivalence or refute sufficiently small local-perturbation theorems.

## Definition

Fix $d\in\{2,5,8\}$ and put
$$SU(d)=\{T\in M_d(\mathbb C):T^*T=I_d,\ \det T=1\}.$$
A **certified $SU(d)$ matrix input** is an exact target $T\in SU(d)$ together
with a deterministic Cauchy-name procedure which, on unary input $1^b$ for
$b\ge1$, returns a rational complex matrix $Q_b$ such that each real and
imaginary coordinate of each entry differs from the corresponding coordinate
of $T$ by at most $2^{-b}$. The interface also specifies a worst-case bit-time
bound $t(b)$ for the query. A **polynomial-time name** has
$t(b)\le(b+1)^c$ for some fixed integer $c\ge1$. The target is the matrix
specified by the entire Cauchy name; if two targets satisfy the same bounds,
every coordinate difference is at most $2^{1-b}$ for all $b$, hence is zero.
No individual $Q_b$ is required to be unitary or special unitary. A requested tolerance is a positive binary
rational and its numerator/denominator encoding length is recorded
separately. For $d=2$ this specializes the unary-name convention of
[[def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input]]. For $d=5,8$ it is the same
entrywise interface in the fixed block dimensions; no dimension is input to
an algorithm as an unbounded parameter.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The target is a fixed d×d matrix with d∈{2,5,8}, and its entire Cauchy-name procedure is supplied, so the input is not an empty family of matrices.
A returned rational coordinate or whole finite approximant may be zero when it satisfies the error bounds; the exact SU(d) target remains unitary and requested tolerance remains positive.
Unary precision b=1 and polynomial exponent c=1 are admitted lower endpoints. Matrix dimension1 is not among{2,5,8}.
Individual Q_b need not be unitary or special unitary, so singular finite approximants are allowed if their coordinate error is certified; the exact target is still inSU(d).
The precision domain explicitly starts at b=1, and dimensions are the fixed set{2,5,8}; b=0 and an unbounded input dimension are not silently admitted.
A deterministic name and its query-time bound are given input data; target uniqueness follows shrinking coordinate bounds without selecting a limiting matrix.

## Statement

Let $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ be unitary operators on the same
finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and suppose
$\|U_j-V_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j\ge0$. With empty
products equal to the identity and empty sums equal to zero,
$$\|U_m\cdots U_1-V_m\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op} \le\sum_{j=1}^m\epsilon_j.$$

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: Current proof1.1 explicitly treats m=0 with I−I=0 and empty error sum0.
All ε_j may be0; the telescope in2.1 then has zero summands. The separate m=0 equality is1.1.
For m=1,2.1 reduces to the single difference U1−V1 with identity outer products, reproducing its input bound.
The estimate does not require distinct factors or strictly positive errors; repeated/identical unitaries give the same finite telescope.
The first/last summands in2.1 use empty outer products asI, consistently with the Statement and m=0 case.
The two finite lists are given and the telescoping sum is an exact algebraic identity; no witnesses are selected.
Individual factor bounds imply a product bound; the reverse fails because different factor errors can cancel in a product.

## Statement

Let $U,V$ be unitary operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let
$\rho$ be any density operator, and let $\mathsf M$ be any finite POVM. If
$\|U-V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$, then the outcome distributions obtained by
measuring $U\rho U^*$ and $V\rho V^*$ have total-variation distance at most
$\epsilon$.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: A density operator has trace1 and therefore lives on a nonzero space; a finite POVM summing toI on it cannot have an empty outcome family.
At ε=0, U=V by the zero operator norm and proof1.1–3.1 gives identical output laws; zero eigenvalue mixture weights in2.1 contribute nothing.
A1-dimensional density space or a one-outcome POVM is allowed; the same trace-distance/measurement inequalities apply and the latter law is deterministic.
A rank-one density is handled directly in1.1; mixed states with zero eigenvalues or repeated eigenvalues are handled by the nonnegative spectral mixture2.1.
The compared U,V are fixed operators, not a time-indexed interpolation; no path endpoint is an input.
Proof2.1 uses a finite orthonormal spectral decomposition of the supplied density matrix; it does not require an arbitrary indexed family choice.
Operator-norm closeness suffices for measurement-law closeness; a single POVM having close laws does not conversely determine an operator-norm bound.

strands, the finite alphabet of positive and inverse Artin generators

of adjacent fusion-measurement locations.

F/R action from the current ordered-list fusion space to the space for the
list with those charges exchanged; track that list after every generator.

[[thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance]]. If a single-space $B_n$ representation is

In the unitary braided fusion category $\mathcal C$ fixed by
[[def-qa-37-anyon-task-and-promise]], use its fixed representative set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Fix $n\ge1$, ordered inputs
$a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$, a total charge

one parenthesized binary tree. Every charge label below belongs to this
same representative set. An **encoded fusion input** consists of the
finite tree shape, a simple-charge label on each internal edge, and a
multiplicity-basis index at each trivalent vertex. A label is **admissible**
exactly when every chosen vertex index belongs to the specified basis of its
multiplicity space $V_{xy}^z$; the allowed local vertex data and resulting
orthonormal fusion-tree vectors are those of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. The input encoding uses fixed self-delimiting
binary codes for charge labels and nonnegative multiplicity indices, with
out-of-range labels rejected as invalid encodings. It also records the total
charge and the selected computational subspace isometry required by
[[def-qa-37-anyon-task-and-promise]], as in
[[def-qc-tqc-fixed-charge-encoding]]. The tree labels and isometry are finite
classical data; they do not themselves specify or prepare the initial encoded
quantum state, which is the separate state/preparation field in the task
record.

## Definition

For a finite anyon solver instance and one run, record separately the tuple
$$\bigl(L_{\rm in},\ N_{\rm any},\ |b|,\ N_{\rm prep},\ N_{\rm anc},\ N_{\rm meas},\ B_{\rm out},\ b_{\max},\ t_{\rm cl},\ T_H,\ \epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},\ p_{\rm leak},\ N_{\rm phase},\ t_{\rm phase}\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm in}$ is the complete finite classical input-description bit
length, including the declared task, state/preparation descriptions when
classically encoded, and tolerance descriptions; a directly supplied quantum
input is not assumed to have a finite classical coordinate description;
