## Definition

For a finite anyon solver instance and one run, record separately the tuple
$$\bigl(L_{\rm in},\ N_{\rm any},\ |b|,\ N_{\rm prep},\ N_{\rm anc},\ N_{\rm meas},\ B_{\rm out},\ b_{\max},\ t_{\rm cl},\ T_H,\ \epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},\ p_{\rm leak},\ N_{\rm phase},\ t_{\rm phase}\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm in}$ is the complete finite classical input-description bit
length, including the declared task, state/preparation descriptions when
classically encoded, and tolerance descriptions; a directly supplied quantum
input is not assumed to have a finite classical coordinate description;
$N_{\rm any}$ is the number of ordered simple-charge strand labels in the
fusion-space instance; and $|b|$ is the number of braid-generator occurrences
(inverse generators count as one). $N_{\rm prep}$ counts elementary
operations in the declared preparation procedure, while $N_{\rm anc}$ counts
the ancillary anyons or other physical ancilla systems used by preparation or
computation. If the initial state is supplied directly as an abstract quantum
input with no preparation interface, $N_{\rm prep}$ is “not applicable”, not
silently set to zero; $N_{\rm anc}$ still records any declared solver ancillas
(zero if none, or “not applicable” if no physical ancilla model is supplied).
$N_{\rm meas}$ is the number of fusion measurements,
and $B_{\rm out}$ is the total bit length of their classical outcome record
under its declared finite encoding (zero when no measurement occurs). The
largest unary precision query to a certified matrix name is $b_{\max}$; $t_{\rm cl}$
is the classical bit time used by search and postprocessing. $T_H$ is the total
Hamiltonian evolution time over the run in the declared physical time unit;
it is “not applicable” for an abstract braid-only model without Hamiltonian
evolution. The error coordinates $\epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},
\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},p_{\rm leak}$ are respectively a stated
operator-norm approximation bound, an independent in-band transport bound,
an implementation-to-ideal-measurement total-variation bound, and leakage
amplitude and probability bounds. $N_{\rm phase},t_{\rm phase}$ count phase
corrections and their classical control cost. Circuit description and
elementary wire costs follow [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]], while classical
input bit cost follows [[def-qa-classical-bit-cost]] and finite nonoracle
gates follow [[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. An inapplicable coordinate is
marked “not applicable”; it is not assigned value zero. Unless an interface
explicitly states a bound, no braid length, preparation operation, ancilla,
matrix precision, measurement, Hamiltonian time, search step, or phase
correction is free. The tuple is a bookkeeping convention; it does not assert
any of its error or runtime bounds.

## Definition

Let $H$ be a fixed finite fusion space with an orthonormal fusion-tree basis
in the category and simple-representative domain of
[[def-qa-37-fusion-input-encoding]]. For a colored task, $H$ is the
currently occupied ordered-list summand tracked by the task record.
For an adjacent pair of leaves or a declared adjacent pair of subtrees, recouple
the tree by its specified unitary $F$-moves so that the pair fuses first. For
each allowed simple total charge $a$ of that pair, let $P_a$ be the orthogonal
projection onto the span of basis vectors whose pair label is $a$, transported
back by the inverse recoupling unitary. Distinct channel subspaces are
orthogonal and their direct sum is $H$, so $(P_a)_a$ is a finite projective
measurement in the sense of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. Its outcome is
$a$, its unnormalized branch vector on input $\psi$ is $P_a\psi$, and the
recoupling follows the inverse-precomposition F convention of
[[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]], whose unitarity is proved in
[[thm-qc-tqc-f-symbol-unitary]]. The branch vector is unnormalized until its probability is checked.

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with $V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, using the
left-associated tree for both fixed-charge spaces. In the ordered list of
$3n$ Fibonacci $\tau$ charges, group consecutive leaves into $n$ triples;
within each triple fuse its first two charges and then its third, and fuse the
$n$ triple outputs by the left-associated $n$-leaf tree to total $c$. Restrict
each triple output to $\tau$; its two local paths are indexed by the charge
$x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two leaves. Fix a rebracketing sequence
of associators from this grouped tree to the fixed left-associated $3n$-leaf
tree, and let $R_{n,c}$ be the induced composite unitary. For each tensor
basis vector $e_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{x_n}\otimes v_\lambda$, where
$e_1,e_\tau$ are the local triple paths and $v_\lambda$ is a basis vector of
$V(\tau^n\to c)$, map it to its grouped fusion-tree basis vector, then
apply $R_{n,c}$. Extend linearly and call the resulting map $J_{n,c}$. Its
image is the code $\mathcal C_{n,c}$ and it is an isometry; set
$P_{n,c}=J_{n,c}J_{n,c}^*$ for the code projector.
The factor $V(\tau^n\to c)$ retains all spectator fusion paths and is not a
physical preparation at zero cost.

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with $V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, using the
left-associated tree for both fixed-charge spaces. In the ordered list of
$3n$ Fibonacci $\tau$ charges, group consecutive leaves into $n$ triples;
within each triple fuse its first two charges and then its third, and fuse the
$n$ triple outputs by the left-associated $n$-leaf tree to total $c$. Restrict
each triple output to $\tau$; its two local paths are indexed by the charge
$x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two leaves. Fix a rebracketing sequence
of associators from this grouped tree to the fixed left-associated $3n$-leaf
tree, and let $R_{n,c}$ be the induced composite unitary. For each tensor
basis vector $e_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{x_n}\otimes v_\lambda$, where
$e_1,e_\tau$ are the local triple paths and $v_\lambda$ is a basis vector of
$V(\tau^n\to c)$, map it to its grouped fusion-tree basis vector, then
apply $R_{n,c}$. Extend linearly and call the resulting map $J_{n,c}$. Its
image is the code $\mathcal C_{n,c}$ and it is an isometry; set
$P_{n,c}=J_{n,c}J_{n,c}^*$ for the code projector.
The factor $V(\tau^n\to c)$ retains all spectator fusion paths and is not a
physical preparation at zero cost.

## Definition

For the fixed Fibonacci convention, write $\rho(b)$ for the physical braid
matrix and $B(b)$ for the normalized word matrix obtained by removing the
common exchange scalar $R_1$ from each Artin generator, as in
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]]. If $e(b)$ is exponent sum, then
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}B(b).$$
On the three-anyon total-$\tau$ block the SK alphabet instead uses the
special-unitary lifts $zB_j$ with $z=e^{3\pi i/10}$, so a word of exponent sum
$k$ satisfies
$$\rho(b)=(R_1z^{-1})^k\widehat B(b),\qquad \widehat B(b)=z^kB(b).$$
A **phase reference record** stores the exact generator scalar, exponent sum,
which normalized convention was compiled, the resulting scalar on each
coherently used branch, and any correction operation and its declared cost
under [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A standalone fixed-sector computation
may report its output projectively using the metric of
[[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]]. In coherent control the active
branch scalar is relative to the inactive branch and must remain in the
record. No phase correction is assigned zero cost unless its interface says
so. This ledger distinguishes the common $R_1^{e(b)}$ phase from the
additional $z^{-e(b)}$ needed when the compiled alphabet is the SU(2) lift.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The empty word has exponent sum0 and both scalar formulas give1; its phase-reference record has no nontrivial word factor.
Zero exponent sum makes the common scalar1, while zero phase-correction count is allowed only when the interface states no correction is performed.
A single signed letter has exponent±1, and the scalar formulas retain its R1 or R1^-1 factor, including the extra lift factor when appropriate.
Standalone projective use may remove one common phase, but coherent control retains it as relative; the Definition does not collapse these two interfaces.
This records algebraic word/branch phases, not geometric crossing endpoints or an adiabatic path.
R1,z and exponent sum fix the scalar exactly; no arbitrary phase reference or free correction operation is selected.
The record distinguishes phase conventions and their costs, without asserting an equivalence between projective gate agreement and equality under coherent control.

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $c\in\{1,\tau\}$, and consider the fixed fusion space
$V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ with its grouped tree of $n$ consecutive triples and
outer triple-charge tree. Its orthogonal decomposition is indexed by local
triple outputs $a_i\in\{1,\tau\}$ and has factors
$$\left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^n V(\tau^3\to a_i)\right) \otimes V(a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\to c),$$
with zero-dimensional summands omitted. A braid word supported on the
internal three strands of the $i$th triple acts on this summand as
$\rho_{a_i}(b)$ on $V(\tau^3\to a_i)$ and the identity on every other local
triple factor and on the outer spectator factor. Reassociating to the fixed
left-associated $3n$-leaf tree conjugates this operator by a unitary; its
operator norm and the stated local-factor action are preserved.

The Statement omits zero-dimensional fusion summands; the local total1 block can be one-dimensional and still has a valid action. Zero block error stayszero under spectator tensoring.
n=1 is admitted; there are no other triple factors and the outer Hom factor is the appropriate scalar simple-sector multiplicity.
The orthogonal direct sum retains all nonzero outer fusion-path multiplicities rather than fixing one spectator state; absent summands do not enter the norm maximum.
The chosen triple may be the first or last one. Proof2.1 leaves every other f_j and the outer g unchanged, so there is no implicit reordering of surrounding strands.
Proof1.1 uses one finite local vertex/path basis and one finite outer-tree basis to identify the complete direct sum; there is no arbitrary infinite family selection.
Local support gives identity action on the stated spectators; the lemma does not assert the converse that every operator acting trivially on those factors is realized by a supported braid.

## Definition

**Inputs:** certified Cauchy names for targets $T_5\in SU(5)$ and
$T_8\in SU(8)$; a positive binary-rational tolerance $\varepsilon$; and the
fixed normalized six-strand Fibonacci B6 generators in both total-charge
blocks. Enumerate all finite Artin words over the six-strand generators and
their inverses, and at stage $s=1,2,\ldots$ inspect every word of length at
most $s$ and every integer precision $1\le p\le s$ not previously inspected,
in fixed lexicographic order. For each word $b$ and precision $p$, compute rational complex
matrix approximants $P_{5,b,p},P_{8,b,p}$ to its exact normalized block
matrices and request rational target approximants $Q_{5,p},Q_{8,p}$. Each
real and imaginary entry error in these approximants is certified at most
$2^{-p}$. For $d\in\{5,8\}$ compute the rational number
$$s_{d,b,p}=\sum_{i,j}\Bigl(|\Re(P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p})_{ij}| +|\Im(P_{d,b,p}-Q_{d,p})_{ij}|\Bigr).$$
Return the first word for which both rational tests
$$s_{d,b,p}+4d\,2^{-p}<\varepsilon\qquad(d=5,8)$$
hold. Output the word, its exponent sum, both rational certificates, and the
measured search/precision costs in the ledger of
[[def-qa-37-resource-cost-model]]. The braid matrices have computable
algebraic entries from the fixed Fibonacci $F/R$ data
[[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-and-artin]]. This is a dovetailed
partial search definition: no cutoff or useful word-length/time bound is
asserted here. A separate theorem in this pair proves termination under certified target
access. The returned matrices are
normalized by the common $R_1$ scalar; their physical phase is recorded by
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]].

$\epsilon_{\rm op}=\varepsilon$, $N_{\rm meas}=B_{\rm out}=0$, and
$N_{\rm phase}=t_{\rm phase}=0$ because it performs no measurement or phase
correction. Preparation, ancilla, Hamiltonian-time, transport, measurement-
implementation and physical-leakage coordinates are “not applicable” because
this mathematical search supplies no physical realization. $L_{\rm in}$,
$|b|$, $b_{\max}$, and $t_{\rm cl}$ record the encoded target/compiler inputs,
returned word, greatest precision request, and measured search/postprocessing
bit time.

A **finite adiabatic braid input** consists of a finite-dimensional complex
Hilbert space $V$, a $C^2$ Hermitian path $H(s)$ on $0\le s\le1$, a
norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ onto a
coherently followed band with uniform positive full gap, a slow-time schedule
$T>0$, and an explicit initial isometry $A_0:\mathbb C^m\to\operatorname{ran}P(0)$.
These are the path and propagator hypotheses of
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]; the output propagator $U_T$ solves
$iU_T'(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$. Also supply an endpoint isometry
$A_1:\mathbb C^m\to\operatorname{ran}P(1)$ and a specified Fibonacci braid
word $b$ with physical action $\rho(b)$ from
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]] in the fixed convention of
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]], and a unitary target
$\rho_{\rm log}(b)\in U(\mathbb C^m)$ in the declared logical input/output
frames. The target $\rho_{\rm log}(b)$ is the selected categorical $F/R$
action written in those frames, including the phase convention recorded by
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]]; specifying it does not assert that the
physical path realizes it. The **in-band transport condition** is the separate
hypothesis
$$\|P(1)U_T(1)A_0-A_1\rho_{\rm log}(b)\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm tr}.$$
This condition is not a consequence of a projector-leakage estimate. The
model also specifies a finite output measurement and, if needed, its own
implementation-variation bound. The JRS expression and leakage consequence
are handled as a separate result.

## Statement

For every Fibonacci braid word $b$ with exponent sum $k$, its physical
operator differs from the normalized operator by the common scalar
$R_1^k$ on every fixed-charge block. On the three-anyon SU(2)-lift alphabet
$zB_j$, the corresponding scalar is $(R_1z^{-1})^k$. The scalar leaves
uncontrolled fixed-sector measurement probabilities unchanged; under a
coherent control it is a relative phase and cannot be discarded without a
phase-reference correction.

A zero exponent sum gives both common phase factors1, including nonempty balanced words.
For one signed generator the scalar contribution is R1^±1 and the SU2-lift correction contributes z^∓1 in1.1.
The generator phases R1,z have modulus1 and never vanish, so inverse letters and normalization are always defined.
This is an algebraic finite-word identity independent of spelling, not a path-endpoint or motion-holonomy claim.
All phase factors are multiplied from the given word; no arbitrary lift or phase correction is selected.
Standalone scalar-phase invariance is not asserted equivalent to coherent-control invariance; the latter distinction is the content of the conclusion.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every certified Cauchy input pair
$(T_5,T_8)\in SU(5)\times SU(8)$ and every positive rational
$\varepsilon$, the exhaustive compiler of
[[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]] halts with one six-strand
Fibonacci braid word whose normalized total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
matrices are each within operator norm $\varepsilon$ of $T_5,T_8$,
respectively. Density proves termination, but this result gives no useful
joint-block word-length or search-time bound.

The search is dovetailed over unbounded stages rather than a fixed final cutoff;2.1 proves some finite stage and precision are eventually reached.
Proof1.1 chooses one finite braid word in the nonempty joint-density neighborhood under ACω;2.1 then chooses one sufficiently large finite precision.

## Statement

For a finite adiabatic braid input with rank-$m$ spectral band and schedule
$T>0$, define
$$A_m(s)=\frac1T\left[\frac{m\|H'(0)\|}{g(0)^2} +\frac{m\|H'(s)\|}{g(s)^2} +\int_0^s\left(\frac{m\|H''(r)\|}{g(r)^2} +\frac{7m\sqrt m\|H'(r)\|^2}{g(r)^3}\right)dr\right].$$
Then
$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s)$, and every unit initial band
vector has leakage probability at most $A_m(s)^2$. In particular,
$\|[I-P(1)]U_T(1)A_0\|_{\rm op}\le A_m(1)$ and leakage probability is at
most $A_m(1)^2$. This result does not prove the separate in-band transport
condition or identify band transport with Fibonacci $F/R$ data.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: A supplied unit initial band vector and preparation isometry require a nonzero band for the transition-probability assertion; an empty prepared state is not an input.
At s=0 the projector difference is exactly0 and the integral is empty. If the path derivatives vanish, the displayed A_m bound is0 while g and T remain positive.
A rank-one spectral band m=1 is included by the same displayed rank-dependent JRS formula and the isometry argument2.1.
The full spectral gap is uniformly positive and band rank is constant; a gap closing or a rank-changing spectral projection is not covered.
Proof1.1 applies the projector estimate on[0,1];2.1 explicitly substitutes the prepared unit vector at s=1 and takes the supremum for the stated endpoint leakage norm.
The path and band are given;2.1 quantifies all unit input vectors and takes a norm supremum, without selecting a basis of band states.
The theorem bounds leakage from spectral following hypotheses; no converse identifies in-band transport or a material Fibonacci realization from a small leakage number.

## Statement

Let $A_0$ and $A_1$ be the initial and endpoint isometries in a finite
adiabatic braid input, let $V$ be the ideal logical unitary, and let $W_c$ be
a compiled logical unitary. Suppose
$$\|W_c-V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_c,\qquad \|P(1)U_T(1)A_0-A_1V\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm tr},$$
and let the JRS leakage amplitude be bounded by $A_m(1)$. Fix a finite POVM $\mathsf M$ on the physical output space. If the
implemented measurement distribution differs from the distribution of this
same $\mathsf M$ on $U_T(1)A_0\rho A_0^*U_T(1)^*$ by at most $\epsilon_m$
in total variation, then for every input density operator $\rho$ the total
measured-output variation from the ideal compiled output
$A_1W_c\rho W_c^*A_1^*$ is at most
$$\epsilon_c+\epsilon_{\rm tr}+A_m(1)+\epsilon_m.$$
The transport mismatch is an explicit independent premise; the JRS estimate
bounds leakage only.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The input density and endpoint isometries concern a nonzero prepared code; a POVM on that nonzero space is not an empty outcome family.
Any or all of ε_c,ε_tr,A_m(1),ε_m may be0;1.1–3.1 adds those nonnegative bounds and gives exact agreement if their sum is0.
A1-dimensional logical input or rank-one density is permitted;2.1 starts with pure states and extends by finite spectral mixing.
Zero eigenvalue mixture weights and a zero leakage operator contribute0 in2.1; no strictly positive errors or full-rank density are required.
Proof1.1 uses S=U_T(1)A0, Tc=A1Wc and Q=I−P(1), retaining the independently supplied initial/endpoint frames.
The only spectral decomposition is finite in2.1; no new physical implementation or phase-matching witness is selected by the budget proof.
The independent error hypotheses imply a measured-output upper bound; a small measured difference is not claimed to imply each component bound or correct transport holonomy.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use the six-anyon triple-triple encoding
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]. For any $U\in U(4)$ put
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For every $\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid word $b$ has both block
errors $\|B_1(b)-T_1\|_{\rm op}<\delta$ and
$\|B_\tau(b)-T_\tau\|_{\rm op}<\delta$. In either total-charge block, the
normalized braid's logical block error and leakage amplitude relative to the
encoded action of $U$ are at most $\delta$. The physical categorical braid is
$\zeta B(b)$ with $\zeta=R_1^{e(b)}$; its logical block error is at most
$\delta$ relative to the phase-matched target $\zeta U$, and its leakage
amplitude is unchanged. This common scalar is recorded under
[[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]] and must be handled under coherent control.
When the two determinant-corrected targets are supplied as certified Cauchy
inputs, the dovetailed B6 compiler finds such a word. No useful joint-block
word-length or search-time bound is asserted.

## Definition

A **physical realization record** for a mathematical braid-compilation
instance contains, in addition to its finite fusion input and braid word, all
of: a specified physical state space and low-energy-sector identification; a
$C^2$ Hermitian path and constant-rank uniformly gapped projection; an
initial preparation isometry and its cost; a slow-time schedule; an endpoint
frame; a separately justified identification of band transport with the
logical-frame Fibonacci $F/R$ target of
[[def-qa-37-finite-adiabatic-braid-input]], including its phase; and a
locality model for exchanges. A local-Hamiltonian model specifies a finite
lattice $\Lambda$ with its metric, an interaction range $R$, and a uniform
per-site interaction bound $J$ for a decomposition
$H(s)=\sum_{X\subseteq\Lambda}h_X(s)$: every $h_X(s)$ is Hermitian and
supported on $X$, $\operatorname{diam}(X)\le R$, and
$$\sup_{s\in[0,1],\,x\in\Lambda}\sum_{X\ni x}\|h_X(s)\|\le J.$$
The record separately states the local-indistinguishability and stability
criteria, including their region scales, norms, tolerances, and the evidence
used to establish them. It also supplies explicit preparation, excitation,
measurement, and control-error terms.
The first spectral-path clauses are the finite interface in
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]] and
[[def-qa-37-finite-adiabatic-braid-input]]. The error ledger is
[[lem-qa-37-total-error-budget]]. A successful SK compilation, projective
density theorem, or JRS leakage estimate supplies none of the material,
locality, preparation, or band-holonomy evidence by itself; those are
independent record fields, not consequences of the mathematical compiler.
Only terms appearing as hypotheses in the stated error ledger contribute to
its measured-output bound; a separately recorded preparation, excitation, or
control error requires an additional bound before it can be included in a
total physical error claim.

## Definition

**Inputs:** a positive binary-rational tolerance $0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$;
the fixed inverse-closed Fibonacci alphabet $G_{\rm Fib}$; and a fixed
certified base-net certificate $(\mathcal N_0,\eta_0,L_0)$ with
$0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$. Select exactly one target interface:

1. **Ideal exact-real interface:** supply an exact-real handle for
   $S\in SU(2)$ with exact fixed-dimensional matrix operations and exact
   comparisons. Invoke the ideal recursive procedure
   [[alg-qc-solovay-kitaev-unitary-compiler]] on $S$ and $\varepsilon$.
2. **Finite Turing interface:** supply a polynomial-time Cauchy name for
   $S\in SU(2)$ and the minimal-polynomial and rational isolating-interval
   descriptions of every real and imaginary gate coordinate required by the
   finite-precision theorem. Run the deterministic Turing implementation
   established by [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]] on that name,
   alphabet, certificate, and tolerance. This branch uses its certified
   interval decisions and does not invoke exact-real comparisons.

In either branch, return the resulting word in the labels
$zB_1,zB_2,(zB_1)^{-1},(zB_2)^{-1}$, its expanded length, and its Artin
exponent sum $k$. The base-net list is supplied certificate data; this
algorithm does not compute it from density. A Cauchy name alone is not an
exact-real handle, and the ideal branch makes no finite bit-time claim.

**Output:** a braid word $b$ and ledger scalar $(R_1z^{-1})^k$ such that,
when the algorithm's hypotheses hold, the normalized SU(2) matrix of $b$ is
within the requested tolerance of $S$. Its physical matrix carries the
recorded scalar from [[def-qa-37-phase-reference-cost]].

A target equal to identity inSU2 is an admissible matrix, and a one-letter word is an admissible output; there is no dimension-one target branch.

The tolerance upper endpoint ε=η0 is allowed. Finite gate coordinates retain isolating-interval endpoint/root conditions through the cited implementation.

## Statement

Let $G_{\rm Fib}$ be the fixed Fibonacci SU(2) alphabet with a supplied finite
base-net certificate of radius $0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$ and maximum word length
$L_0$. For every exact target $S\in SU(2)$ and rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, let
$$\eta_{j+1}=64\eta_j^{3/2},\qquad J=\min\{j\ge0:\eta_j\le\varepsilon\}.$$
The ideal SK recursion returns a normalized braid word $W$ with
$\|S-W\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$ and length at most $L_0 5^J$; hence its
length is $O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
If each real and imaginary gate coordinate is supplied by its minimal
polynomial and rational isolating interval with the endpoint/root conditions
of the published finite-precision theorem, the base certificate is fixed,
and $S$ has a polynomial-time Cauchy name with query cost at most $(b+1)^c$,
the finite implementation additionally has the bit-time bound
$O((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10})$ from the cited theorem, where
$N=\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil$ and $s_\varepsilon$ is the binary
encoding length of the rational tolerance. The lifted physical braid carries
$(R_1z^{-1})^k$ and that phase is not part of the normalized error.

## Statement

On one target qubit, $I_2$ and $-I_2$ differ only by a global phase and
induce the same standalone ray and outcome probabilities. Controlled access
changes the comparison. With control first,
$$C(I_2)=I_4,\qquad C(-I_2)=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix} =Z\otimes I_2.$$
On input $|+\rangle|0\rangle$, these give $|+\rangle|0\rangle$ and
$|-\rangle|0\rangle$. Measuring the control in the $X$ basis is
respectively deterministic for $+$ and $-$, so the total-variation distance
is one. Thus projective equivalence of an isolated braid gate is not
interchangeable with equality under coherent control.

The matrices, |+0> input and measurement basis are fixed, so the counterexample is explicit.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$, so it is finite semisimple, rigid, monoidal, and has simple unit [[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects and let $n\ge0$. Fix one representative of each simple isomorphism class for the internal path labels; the external objects $a,b,c$ need not equal their representatives. Set $T_0=b$ and recursively fix the left-associated parenthesization $T_{j+1}:=T_j\otimes a$. The **fixed-boundary anyonic path space** is

$$H_{a,n;b,c}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n).$$

For simple labels $x,y$, define the split multiplicity space $W_{x,a}^y:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(y,x\otimes a)$. For $n\ge1$, a fusion path is a sequence of simple labels $x_0=b,x_1,\ldots,x_n=c$, with $x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}$ drawn from the fixed representative set, together with, for every $1\le j\le n$, one basis index $\mu_j$ in a chosen basis $B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ of $W_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$. The basis index is retained even when distinct indices have the same adjacent labels. Fusion rules are the nonnegative integers $N_{x a}^{y}$ in $[x][a]=\sum_yN_{x a}^{y}[y]$ [[def-fusion-rules]].

For $n=0$, there is no path if $b\not\cong c$. If $b\cong c$, fix an isomorphism $u_{c,b}:c\to b$ and take it as the single empty-path vector (use $u_{b,b}=\operatorname{id}_b$ when the objects coincide). In the unitary setting choose this isomorphism unitary.

For $n\ge1$, if $i_j\in B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ is the selected inclusion $x_j\to x_{j-1}\otimes a$, define the path composite by $\gamma_0:=\operatorname{id}_b$ and $\gamma_j:=(\gamma_{j-1}\otimes\operatorname{id}_a)\circ i_j:x_j\to T_j$. For $x_n=c$, $\gamma_n$ is a vector in $H_{a,n;b,c}$. The next lemma proves these composites form a basis and computes the dimension. No Hilbert-space or physical Hamiltonian structure is part of this definition.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category with unit $\mathbf1$. Its Grothendieck fusion ring $K_0(\mathcal C)$ is the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with multiplication induced by tensor product and coefficients given by the fusion rules of [[def-fusion-rules]].

- An object $X$ is **tensor-invertible** if there is an object $Y$ with $X\otimes Y\cong\mathbf1$ and $Y\otimes X\cong\mathbf1$.
- A class $[X]$ is a **fusion-ring unit** if it has a two-sided multiplicative inverse in $K_0(\mathcal C)$; that inverse may have negative integer coefficients in the simple-object basis.
- A linear operator is **invertible** only relative to a specified vector space $H$ and operator $T:H\to H$: it must have a two-sided inverse $S:H\to H$ with $ST=TS=I_H$.

These definitions concern different objects: categorical tensor product, a ring with virtual classes, and a chosen representation on a vector space.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category with unit $\mathbf1$. Its Grothendieck fusion ring $K_0(\mathcal C)$ is the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with multiplication induced by tensor product and coefficients given by the fusion rules of [[def-fusion-rules]].

- An object $X$ is **tensor-invertible** if there is an object $Y$ with $X\otimes Y\cong\mathbf1$ and $Y\otimes X\cong\mathbf1$.
- A class $[X]$ is a **fusion-ring unit** if it has a two-sided multiplicative inverse in $K_0(\mathcal C)$; that inverse may have negative integer coefficients in the simple-object basis.
- A linear operator is **invertible** only relative to a specified vector space $H$ and operator $T:H\to H$: it must have a two-sided inverse $S:H\to H$ with $ST=TS=I_H$.

These definitions concern different objects: categorical tensor product, a ring with virtual classes, and a chosen representation on a vector space.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$, with pivotal structure and spherical dimension as in [[def-pivotal-structure]], [[def-spherical-structure]], and [[def-the-dimension-of-an-object-relative-to-a-pivotal-structure]]. Let $a$ be a self-dual simple object with $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$. Choose a unit vector $v:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ spanning the one-dimensional vacuum split space and let $d_a>0$ be its positive spherical dimension.

A **normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum** is a supplied pair of maps $\operatorname{coev}:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ and $\operatorname{ev}:a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$ of the form

$$\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt{d_a}\,v,\qquad \operatorname{ev}=\kappa_a\sqrt{d_a}\,v^\dagger,$$

where $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the two duality zig-zag identities hold after the self-duality identification, using the left-dual convention of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]. We call $\kappa_a$ the **Frobenius–Schur sign in this normalized cup/cap convention**. It is not a braiding or $R$-symbol phase.

This item records supplied normalized duality data; it does not assert that every self-dual simple object admits the displayed gauge or prove a trace, ribbon, or category-equivalence theorem. An example must supply the datum or compute the sign from coherent normalized F-data; fusion rules alone do not specify it.

## Definition

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$, chosen from the fixed internal representative set of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Choose bases in the split spaces $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x\otimes y)$ at every vertex of the trees used below, retaining the fixed path vertex bases on the fixed tree. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a typed composite of associators and their inverses carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree, without permuting the ordered inputs (including the boundary charge). In the split-tree bases of $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target coordinates as rows and source coordinates as columns. The proof below constructs these bases and proves invertibility in any complex fusion category. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction. The split Hom convention here is $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. In the unitary case with adjoint vertex bases, each local left-to-right split recoupling matrix is the entrywise conjugate of the QC25 inverse-precomposition F matrix, as proved below; they agree for the displayed real Fibonacci and Ising blocks.

## Statement

Put $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Use $ab=a+b$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$, with summands ordered $(0,1)$ and every nonzero elementary fusion multiplicity equal to one. Let $d=\sqrt2$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$, $\tau=\kappa/d$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$, and choose $\beta$ of modulus one with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. There is a unitary skeletal spherical ribbon fusion category with canonical orthonormal summand vertices and the following complete normal data. All admissible one-dimensional F blocks are $1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$, and
$$F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Rows are right-tree channels $(f,1,1)$ and columns left-tree channels $(e,1,1)$ in the inverse-precomposition convention. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels have the unique empty matrix. The associator permutes the $DD$ summand by addition of a group input when needed; its complete formula and pentagon are proved below.

The object braiding is $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=\beta/u(g)$. The pullback R symbols are their inverses, in the specified canonical vertices. Both hexagons hold in every channel. The normalized self-duality has $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$, $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$, FS sign $\kappa$, positive pivotal dimension $d$, and twist $\theta_D=\kappa/\beta$; $\eta$ has dimension and FS sign one and twist $-1$. The canonical left-dual tensorator is $\kappa$ on both $DD$ channels and one on all other channels; its double-dual tensorator is one on all ten admissible channels. Relative to those duals $j_D=\kappa$, $j_0=j_\eta=1$, and $j_{a\otimes b}=\nu_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ holds channel by channel. For explicit phase specializations write $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. These assertions construct the full category; they do not assume a sector example as a supplier.

## Statement

Put $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Use $ab=a+b$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$, with summands ordered $(0,1)$ and every nonzero elementary fusion multiplicity equal to one. Let $d=\sqrt2$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$, $\tau=\kappa/d$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$, and choose $\beta$ of modulus one with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. There is a unitary skeletal spherical ribbon fusion category with canonical orthonormal summand vertices and the following complete normal data. All admissible one-dimensional F blocks are $1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$, and
$$F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Rows are right-tree channels $(f,1,1)$ and columns left-tree channels $(e,1,1)$ in the inverse-precomposition convention. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels have the unique empty matrix. The associator permutes the $DD$ summand by addition of a group input when needed; its complete formula and pentagon are proved below.

The object braiding is $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=\beta/u(g)$. The pullback R symbols are their inverses, in the specified canonical vertices. Both hexagons hold in every channel. The normalized self-duality has $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$, $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$, FS sign $\kappa$, positive pivotal dimension $d$, and twist $\theta_D=\kappa/\beta$; $\eta$ has dimension and FS sign one and twist $-1$. The canonical left-dual tensorator is $\kappa$ on both $DD$ channels and one on all other channels; its double-dual tensorator is one on all ten admissible channels. Relative to those duals $j_D=\kappa$, $j_0=j_\eta=1$, and $j_{a\otimes b}=\nu_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ holds channel by channel. For explicit phase specializations write $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. These assertions construct the full category; they do not assume a sector example as a supplier.

## Statement

Set $q=e^{\pi i/4}$, $s=e^{\pi i/8}$ and $d=\sqrt2$. The specified rank-one tilting negligible quotient is ribbon-equivalent to the normal-data category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]] at $\kappa=-1$, $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$, with labels $p_0=\mathbf1$, $p_1=D$, $p_2=\eta$. It gives $F_D^{DDD}=-2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, FS sign $-1$, positive dimension $\sqrt2$, and $\theta_D=s^3$.

Multiplying the associator by $\omega(x,y,z)=(-1)^{|x||y||z|}$ and the braiding by $(-i)^{|x||y|}$, with $D$ odd and group objects even, gives the distinct $\kappa=+1$, $\beta_+=s$ category. Reversing its braiding and twist is a further explicitly different chirality operation.

## Statement

Use either coherent $\kappa$ category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]], with reference charge $D$ and representative set $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)=\{\mathbf1,\eta,D\}$. For $L\ge1$ define the periodic carrier

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_{b\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)}H_{D,L;b,b},$$

using the fixed-boundary path spaces of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]] and the orthogonal Hilbert direct-sum inner product. The union of their fusion-path bases, supplied as orthonormal bases by [[thm-anyonic-path-space-is-hilbert-under-unitarity]], is the cyclic path basis: a path in the $b$ summand has $x_1=b$, $x_{L+1}=x_1$, and retains every elementary fusion index. Odd $L$ gives the zero space. For $L=2N$, $N\ge1$, this complete orthonormal carrier is $H\oplus\bar H$, each sector of dimension $2^N$, with the explicit bit identifications in the proof. These identifications intertwine every vacuum pair projector, including wraparound:
$$P_{2j-1}|_H=(1+X_j)/2,\quad P_{2j}|_H=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,$$
$$P_{2j-1}|_{\bar H}=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,\quad P_{2j}|_{\bar H}=(1+X_{j+1})/2.$$
All bit indices are modulo $N$. For $N=1$ the bond is the identity; no three-distinct-site cyclic TL assertion is made for this length-two identification.

Let $C|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle=|b_2\cdots b_Nb_1\rangle$, $Q=\prod_jX_j$, and
$$K_{c,b}=2^{-N/2}(-1)^{\sum_jc_j(b_{j-1}+b_j)}.$$
The one-step periodic path shift and the annular line maps defined by the full cyclic F contraction satisfy
$$T=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\I&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y_\eta=\operatorname{diag}(Q,Q),\quad Y_D=\kappa^N\begin{pmatrix}0&K^\dagger\\K&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
They obey $TP_iT^{-1}=P_{i-1}$, $Y_D^2=I+Y_\eta$, $Y_\eta^2=I$, $Y_\eta Y_D=Y_DY_\eta=Y_D$, and each line map commutes with every represented $P_i$ and with $T$. In contrast the specified normalized single-chain map obeys $(K/\sqrt2)^2=(I+Q)C^{-1}/2$. The proof supplies all wrapping, kernel, rank, Hamiltonian, and intertwining assertions on the full two-sector space, without a total-flux or global-spin-parity projection.
